title: Half treble
subtitle: The middle-height stitch, called half double crochet in the United States
excerpt: The half treble sits between the double crochet and the treble in height. One yarn-over, then all three loops come off together. It gives a warm, slightly dense fabric with a little more give than double crochet, which makes it a favourite for hats and blankets.
sourceNotes: Reconstructed in our own words from Thérèse de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), Chapter 9 (Crochet Work), the passage on half trebles (Fig. 415). Public domain via Project Gutenberg. UK and US stitch-name equivalences cross-checked against the Craft Yarn Council standard terms.

glossaryTerms.definition: A crochet stitch worked with one yarn-over, then finished by pulling through all three loops at once. It stands between double crochet and treble in height. The UK name; the same stitch is called half double crochet in the United States.
The United States name for the stitch British patterns call a half treble. The working steps are identical; only the name differs.
Wrapping the working yarn over the hook from back to front before working a stitch. A half treble takes one wrap before the hook goes in.

content.text: Begin with one working loop on the hook.
Wrap the yarn over the hook once.
Insert the hook into the next stitch or chain.
Wrap the yarn over and draw a loop back through. Three loops now sit on the hook.
Wrap the yarn over once more and pull through all three loops together. One loop is left, and the half treble is done.
At the start of a row, two chains usually stand in for the first half treble.

The half treble is a favourite for hats, mittens, cowls, and baby blankets, where you want a fabric warmer and denser than treble but quicker and softer than double crochet. It works up fast and has a pleasant texture, with that small ridge along the top of each row. Many simple beanie patterns are nothing but rounds of half treble.

Working into the third loop, the strand that sits behind the usual top, gives a smooth knit-like line popular for brims. The double crochet is the shorter neighbour; the treble is the taller one. Two half trebles worked together make a soft decrease. The stitch responds well to a slightly larger hook when you want more drape.
Difficulty: beginner. A natural next step once double crochet and treble feel comfortable.
